paper.abstract_en: Cosmological inflation provides the standard description of the early accelerated expansion of the Universe, but the shortcomings of General Relativity (GR) motivate the search for alternative gravitational frameworks. In this paper, we study inflation in $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ gravity, constructed in the symmetric teleparallel formulation, where the non-metricity scalar $Q$ couples non-minimally to the matter Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_m$. We consider an inflaton scalar field with a power-law potential and show that, in this framework, the inflationary dynamics is governed by the interplay between the scalar field and the effective geometric sector generated by the matter-geometry coupling. Thus, the scalar field supplies the matter source, while the modified $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)$ structure alters the background evolution and the inflationary observables. Within the slow-roll approximation, we derive the expressions of the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ for both linear and nonlinear coupling models. The linear model, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)=-αQ+2\mathcal{L}_m+β$, is treated as a benchmark GR-like limit, whereas the nonlinear model, $f(Q,\mathcal{L}_m)=-αQ+(2\mathcal{L}_m)^2+β$, captures the genuinely modified effects of the theory. We find that the linear model remains consistent with the latest joint Planck 2018 and BICEP/Keck (BK18) constraints ($r < 0.036$ at $95\%$ CL) for positive $α$ and $β$, while the nonlinear model is favored for negative values of these parameters and yields predictions largely concentrated within the $68\%$ confidence level. These results indicate that the nonlinear matter-geometry coupling can lead to distinct inflationary behavior and may improve the observational compatibility of the quadratic potential $(n=2)$, which is strongly disfavored in the standard GR-based inflationary scenario.
